speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On such journeys, when you have young kids like my wife and I, there are certain things we will never forget to bring.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And for Poppy, you guess it – there is her LOL doll.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There was a time when my daughters each received different toys and they would bicker over who gets what.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Then, one day, my eldest daughter Ella told me, "Daddy, why do not you just give us the same toys so we do not need to quarrel anymore?" Wise advice from that little one that I gladly followed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But there is something more important than anything else to bring, even these dolls and, that is, our child car seats, enough for all three of our girls.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A few years back, a young mother sat in the passenger seat of a car, cradling her child in her arms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was a day of perfect road conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The sky was clear, the roads were dry and the traffic was light.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The child fractured her skull, bled from her nose and mouth and faced severe brain damage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And after three days on life support, the child passed away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I spoke to A&E and Neonatal ICU doctors, and they shared with me many more such stories, whose details are too gory for this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They all tell me: a child car seat could have made a difference.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I will offer four recommendations that will make taxi and PHC rides safer for the children of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: LTA is already working hard on this issue of child car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have consulted with stakeholders and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But as they have shared, opinions are "very divided" and a compromise remains elusive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To build a compromise, I spent months speaking with LTA, parents, taxi drivers, PHC drivers, doctors and other members of the public and Taxi Baby, an organisation involved in child car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am also a parent who brings child car seats onto taxis and PHCs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My wife does not have a driving licence and relies on public transport, so we, too, understand the difficulties and the trade-offs involved.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Were my kids screaming when put in child car seats initially?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But if we start them in the child car seats as newborns, they will get used to it quite quickly and the screaming stops.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Most importantly, will it significantly lower the risks of injury and death during accidents?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They understand why we want to and they are supportive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am speaking up about this so that no one lives in regret – not the child who faces serious injury or death, not the parents who wish they could have done more, and not the taxi and PHC drivers who will have to live with the guilt.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Since it is given free, passengers should be able to use them for free, too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Child car seats are extremely effective at protecting children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Doctors at our own KKH found that a child not in a child car seat was 8.4 times more likely to be seriously injured in a road accident.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I respect our taxi drivers, but they are not immune to something going wrong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MOT data shows that, on average, taxis are involved in about three injury-causing accidents daily.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Children can and do ride taxis and they need to be protected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, LTA ran a pilot with SMRT where all of SMRT taxis were equipped with one child car seat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am suggesting we do things differently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The SMRT pilot provided one seat only for children aged four and above.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By contrast, my proposal with two seats covers children of nearly every age.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As each family has an average of two children in Singapore, this will help a good proportion of families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The SMRT pilot was also limited to just one company.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My proposal allows parents to continue taking the taxi or PHC service of their choice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One night, having travelled out on an MRT, she decided to return home in a taxi.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She normally brings child car seats, but this ride was unplanned.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, since it was also just a short journey, she held her daughter in her arms and sat her son next to her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This one time that she did not use child car seats was the one time that she got into an accident.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Her daughter was flung out of her arms and fell on the floor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She shared with me that she always thought she could hold on to her daughter if an accident like that happened.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By a stroke of luck, the kids did not suffer serious injuries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents may think that an accident would not happen that one time that they do not put their child in a child car seat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents may think that they can hold to their child in an accident.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Eva's story shows, accidents can happen to anybody and when it strikes, no parent can be 100% sure that they can hold on and protect their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For parents like Eva, my proposal means they will need to carry fewer or even no child car seats when going out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When it comes to child car seats, convenience means safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second benefit of my proposal is lower costs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mr Baey points out, low costs for parents should be a priority in this pandemic economy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He pointed to existing ride options that already provide child car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A GrabFamily car costs more, sometimes much more, than a typical Grab ride and is harder to find.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By contrast, my proposal allows parents to use child car seats at no costs and they can shop for the cheapest taxi or PHC provider they can find.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nothing keeps costs low like good old market competition after all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The third benefit of my proposal is fewer driver-passenger conflicts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ask any PHC driver and they will tell you stories about driving a long way to the pick-up point, only to find that the passenger has brought their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These drivers have to turn the passengers away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They ask, "How come I can bring my child in a taxi but not your car?" My proposal makes this a non-issue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Every taxi and PHC will have child car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is no reason for any driver to turn away any parent anymore or risk breaking the law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All taxis and PHC drivers will have an increased customer base and can potentially earn more because of this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: PHC drivers will also be happy to spend less time travelling to passengers they cannot pick up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents will be happy to avoid wasting their own time and money.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And because everyone is happy, I am sure MOT will be happy too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At this stage, I have talked a lot about the benefits.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Taxis and PHCs have to carry whatever barang barang commuters bring.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How can they squeeze two child car seats into storage?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today's child car seats are not just the large clunky ones you have known for decades.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can see for yourself how small they are: this child car seat is for children aged nine months to four years old and this seat is for those aged four years old and above.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Taxi and PHC drivers were shocked when I showed them these car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One fits in a glove compartment and the other barely takes up any space in the boot.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I have shown in the video on my social media platforms, they fit with more than enough room left in the boot for two suitcases.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The space concerns become minimal, even for hybrid cars.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The next concern I have heard is about time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would not car seats take a long time to assemble?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You can see the video on my social media platforms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is faster than helping a passenger in a wheelchair to board a taxi and not much longer than helping passengers with many bags arrange them in the boot.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The third and final concern is about costs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, how much will it cost to deck an island of taxis and PHCs with these child car seats?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Here is the exact quotation I have got for MOT.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have addressed it to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey but he tells me I should address it to MOF as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This amount is not a lot, compared to similar projects.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will also add that this cost-benefit analysis needs to go beyond the cost of these seats themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Tammie, a physiotherapist, shared with me on Facebook, we must "spend a few days in a traumatic head injury or spinal chord injury rehabilitation ward to understand true cost.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How do you cost the loss of vocation, loss of bladder control, loss of memory, loss of executive functioning, loss of time, loss of potential and the resultant burden on families?” This brings me to my second proposal.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second proposal is to launch an awareness campaign.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This campaign would focus on two things: one, the universal availability of child car seats in taxis and PHCs; and two, the critical importance of using these seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many parents do not know that child car seats are important.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is not hard to guess what went through those parents' minds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I recall when we drove up to Cameron Highlands years ago.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ella, then a little baby, cried almost the entire way in her child car seat.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She hated the idea of sitting anywhere other than on Mommy and Daddy's lap.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Sometimes, the most instinctive thing for a parent to do is to hold their child tight.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I can hardly blame anyone for this instinct.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we must do what is right for our children, not just what feels right.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must build a culture where child car seats are always used.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not just sometimes, not just occasionally, but always.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My proposal of providing child car seats to taxis and PHCs would be a key part of this awareness campaign.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government could tie up with taxi operators, ride-hailing companies, the National Taxi Association and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There could be joint marketing campaigns – from banners on our streets to notifications on apps to in-vehicle stickers for raising awareness on child car seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As an added bonus, helping parents learn about child car seats in taxis and PHCs will also encourage them to use them in their own cars, if they eventually buy one.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hospitals should include in the prenatal classes lessons on how to use infant car seats, just like how they teach parents how to safely carry, feed, bathe and change infants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH) already includes a child car seat in its packing checklist for parents admitting for delivery.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After all, most infants are brought home from hospitals in cars.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What precedent does it set if the very first car ride does not involve an infant car seat?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are easy to carry and can fit easily onto a stroller.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hospitals can sell these to parents who do not have infant car seats ready at the point of discharge.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government can facilitate a pilot like this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, with a public tender and buying in bulk, I am sure the price will be even cheaper.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The price of these seats can also be added to the hospital bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should study their experiences and apply their learnings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let that not stop us from taking action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fellow Member of Parliament and Advisor to the National Taxi Association and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, shared their feedback with me.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The drivers and associations are supportive of this move to ensure the safety of our young families in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Having these options will expand the ridership base for both our taxi and private hire drivers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, she also noted that there are some operational and safety constraints, such as maintaining the cleanliness of child car seats, disinfecting these seats to ensure high standards of hygiene and the time taken to set up these seats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are valid concerns and I welcome feedback from all stakeholders to refine the proposals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we all share the same concerns for the safety of our children, I have no doubt that we can work together to find a feasible arrangement which addresses the operational and safety concerns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to further dialogues with the associations, LTA and other stakeholders to strengthen the proposals and make our journeys safer for our children while taking into account the various trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We decided to exempt taxis from child car seats a few decades ago.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Child car seat technology has improved drastically since then.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2006, the idea of installing seat belts in school buses was raised in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government then replied, let us think carefully about this; after all, there has been no serious injuries for the past six years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But just two years later, a boy was flung out of a school bus and died.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Within the year, we mandated the installation of seat belts in school buses and funded it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us not wait for another young one to be hurt before we take action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a matter of when, not if.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do not just take it from me as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Assoc Prof Chong Shu-Ling from the Department of Emergency Medicine at KKH said, "Just as we would spare nothing to give our children the best, we must endeavour to put them in appropriate car restraints to protect them in the event of a road collision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must choose to avoid death and permanent brain damage that can occur if an unrestrained child gets seriously hurt." Another doctor from KKH, Dr Nirmal Visruthan said, "Motor vehicular incidents can be especially traumatic in infants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Using an appropriate car restraint reduces this risk several folds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They can be flung from the car seat if unrestrained and develop head injuries which can cause brain damage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a parent and paediatrician, it is hard for me to see the children deteriorate or die from these severe injuries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The parents too may suffer from massive guilt of disregarding the importance of strapping them in." Madam, I join the doctors and many others in calling for this important change that will help save lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It can only be understood by knowing and feeling the pain, anguish, depression and shattered hopes of the victims and of wives, husbands, parents, children, grandparents and friends."

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I also have three kids, but we never bought three sets of toys for our kids because we believe that they should learn to share.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Member has raised several Parliamentary Questions before on the topic of making child seats mandatory in taxis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In fact, it was the Member who first gave the idea for SMRT's booster seat trial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We also enjoyed the video he made with his two adorable daughters and shared on social media.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Therefore, we have introduced many measures to protect the safety of motorists, their passengers and other road users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These include good traffic rules, stringent standards in awarding driving and vocational licences, effective traffic management systems and enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our practice is similar to countries, such as Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and some jurisdictions in the US, including New York and Washington DC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Member is right that places like Germany, California and New South Wales strictly require child restraints and booster seats to be used in taxis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, in these places, the onus is generally on the parents to bring along the required types and number of child restraints and booster seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Taxis there are, generally, not required to provide the child restraints and booster seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the years, there have been concerns about bulky child seats taking up significant boot space in taxis and the time taken to install and remove them for each trip.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As children of different age groups require different types of restraints and seats, there were also concerns about how to ensure that taxis had the right configuration of child seats to cater to different families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The alternative was for parents to be responsible for providing the child seats, as is the practice in some countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But there were practical challenges about parents having to lug heavy, bulky car seats around, especially those with bigger families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As the Member has rightly pointed out, more portable child restraints and seats have become available on the market in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At that time, we had also sought public and industry feedback on the option of mandating the use of child restraints and booster seats in taxis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, views were split almost right down the middle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even within each group of stakeholders consulted, there were different views.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some parents felt that they are fundamentally responsible for their child's safety and should be able to decide whether to bring and use child restraints and booster seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even if taxis and PHCs are equipped with child restraints and booster seats, some parents also voiced concerns regarding their hygiene and may prefer not to use them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I expect the concerns to be greater now during the current pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Larger families will also have to divide themselves into multiple vehicles as the carrying capacity of taxis will be reduced with child restraints and booster seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, a family with two adults and three children can commute in one taxi now.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I believe this applies to the Member's family as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Taxi drivers also raised concerns about mandating child seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Because of the "flag and go" nature of street-hail trips, it is not possible for commuters to indicate their requirements for child restraints and booster seats in advance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Drivers expressed concerns about their own safety and causing traffic tailbacks and unhappiness from other road users as they set up the child restraints and booster seats by the side of the road.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Member mentioned that setting up child restraints and booster seats takes less time than helping a passenger in a wheelchair to board a taxi.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Passengers in foldable wheelchairs typically board on the side of the street.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are helped on board, the wheelchair is folded and stowed in the boot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Child restraints and booster seats are quite different.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If there are more than one child restraint and/or booster seats, one of them would have to be set up on the side of the road.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The parent would also have to squeeze in between the two children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I note that the Member has not shown us his trick in his video of how he managed to squeeze in between his two kids on their booster seats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While models proposed by the Member are portable, they are for children who are about nine months or older.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Child seats for young infants still tend to be bulkier and more expensive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, we will work with the operators to review how the Member's suggestion will affect the remaining boot space for other passengers, such as those with foldable wheelchairs or luggage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our point-to-point transport operators are sensitive to the market and greater demand for child restraints and booster seats from parents will spur operators to increase the provision.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In fact, SMRT has already conducted a booster seat trial, which the Member is familiar with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, looking at the SMRT trial, the issue is not just about the provision of child restraints and booster seats but also how to raise awareness and ensure that parents use the child restraints and booster seats when they are provided.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is the Member's second recommendation, which we fully support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the issue of child seats, parents, drivers and operators all need to be on board.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, raising awareness and reaching a common understanding is key.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will be happy to work with the Member to engage the relevant agencies and stakeholders.
